note: Goals of the laws in a series: crime in general gives criminal_justice list (5.2) and peace in an enumeration is list (4.10).
Torture and executions are named as human-rights violations with no custody or police element; peace appears only as a general aim.
Organized crime corrupting and infiltrating the State carries the point of its sentence, so corruption applies; drugs, trafficking in humans and illegal mining are items of one enumeration.
Release of hostages demanded alongside the ceasefire, with no sentence about the taking itself: peace only (5.2, row (b)).
IUU fishing is named only as an economic threat and waste discharge as one pollution problem among others (4.8, 5.2).
The investigation of the miners' massacre is enforcement against this crime, so criminal_justice is not added (4.9).
The ban on laundering drug proceeds is the subject of a sentence (5.1); mutual legal assistance against drugs gives drugs only.
'Cross-border crime' read as transnational crime, organized_crime list (5.2); funding of African peace support operations gives peace.
'Reign of terror' is an epithet for the former regime; no war, custody or peace process is discussed in the fragment.
The anti-corruption conference Belgium organized is the point of its sentence, not a mere name.
Illicit finance and illicit small arms share one claim in a series (3.2); the Security Council's shortcomings as a tool give peace.
Peace appears only as the Organization's purpose and an aspiration (4.10); murder and torture are human-rights concerns without a justice-system element.
The illicit small arms trade and transnational crime share one claim of support in a series (3.2); implementing the Charter's collective security system gives peace.
The maintenance of international peace and security appears only as one of the Charter's ends in an enumeration (4.10).
Non-use of force and peaceful settlement of disputes appear only as items in an enumeration of Charter principles (4.10); 'hostage' is a metaphor.
Apartheid, calls to isolate the regime and to release political prisoners carry no lens (4.9, 4.10); detention appears only as a means.
Torture is addressed as a human-rights practice with no custody or police element (4.9).
Migrant workers' rights instruments carry no lens.
Access to justice for survivors of sexual violence is a criminal-justice element (4.9); the women, peace and security agenda is one end of a series.
'International crime' refers to aggression, not criminal_justice.
The small arms conference is not described as about illicit trade, so peace only (4.4); the terrorism convention is one item in a series of means.
Judicial reform, decriminalized press offences and abolition of the death penalty as criminal justice policy (death penalty at confidence 2 per the YAML).
Groups designated as terrorists and narco-terrorism give terrorism and drugs; the declared non-international armed conflict gives peace; youth violence prevention gives criminal_justice.
Support for terrorists and respect for the neighbours' sovereignty are demands in a series addressed to one State (3.2, 4.6); the deal's subject is not stated.
Scams by organized crime give organized_crime; 'crime' in the closing antithesis refers back to them, so criminal_justice is not added.
Arbitrary detention and sexual violence are named as abuses under occupation, which give peace, not criminal_justice (4.9).
The abduction issue is presented as a human-rights violation with no takers or demand described, so no terrorism.
Peace appears only as one of the Organization's pillars in an enumeration (4.10); torture is named as a human-rights violation.
'Petty crime' is crime in general (5.2); 'war' and 'terror' are said of criminal organisations, so no peace or terrorism.
Peace appears only as the Organization's purpose; the unilateral embargo is neither an armed conflict nor a Security Council measure (4.10).
'Accomplices in crime' is invective; aggression is condemned in general, with no specific conflict.
IUU fishing is framed as a threat to stocks, the economy and regional security, with no criminal groups, prosecution or penalties (4.8).
'Security' in the list of areas is too vague for criminal_justice.
Terrorism appears only as the standard of comparison in a subordinate clause (3.2).
Making peace in the speaker's region and preventing conflict are concrete; torture by Governments is an atrocity, not criminal_justice.
Drug abuse is named only as the problem, with no prevention or treatment response (5.2).
'Criminal' sanctions and 'aggression' are invective for unilateral sanctions; no armed conflict or Security Council measure.
'Fraudulent and uncontrolled trade in weapons' read as illicit arms trade (4.4); disarmament and a code for arms sales between States give peace.
The country's emergence from a ten-year armed struggle into peace gives peace; the children's abduction is not framed as exploitation, so no trafficking.
Punishment of war criminals is international criminal justice, outside criminal_justice; the Second World War it concerns gives peace.
Torture is named among human-rights denials, with no custody or police element (4.9).
Crime in general and peace appear only as items of enumerations (5.2, 4.10).
Human trafficking, money laundering and illegal mining are items of one enumeration of distinct crimes; dismantling transnational gangs gives organized_crime.
The sentence linking drug trafficking to crime in general gives criminal_justice (5.2).
Enumeration of threats sharing one cause: common criminality gives criminal_justice, cross-border crimes organized_crime and insurgency peace, all list.
Laws on sexual offences give criminal_justice (4.9); resolution 1325 on women, peace and security gives peace.
Mobilizing at the Crime Congress and the organized crime symposium for a preventive strategy and structures against terrorism and organized crime; drug trafficking is only an example.
Political prisoners appear only in an aside about the former regime, not as conditions of detention (4.9); peace here is domestic reconciliation.
The sentence is about the outcome of the review conference on the illicit small arms trade, so organized_crime applies (4.4); its effect on disarmament gives peace.
Ship seizures by the Kuomintang forces are acts of an armed party called 'piratical' as invective, so peace only (4.4, 4.6).
Aggressors disguising conquest as 'special military operations' is an identifiable aggression (4.10).
Terrorism, violent extremism and conflicts are items of one enumeration of challenges.
Sentences linking terrorism to crime and delinquency in general give both lenses (5.2).
Illicit small arms trade is organized_crime whoever receives the weapons; no sentence treats disarmament or a conflict (4.4).
Drug addiction is named only as the problem, and extradition against traffickers gives drugs only (5.1, 5.2).
The campaign against small arms trafficking gives organized_crime (4.4); the sentence on such weapons encouraging terrorism gives terrorism.
Hijacking counts by its kind but is one item of a series of violent acts (4.6, 3.2); governments' duty to prevent crime and bring criminals before the law gives criminal_justice.
The Commission on Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice appears only as the body drafting the organized crime convention, so criminal_justice is not added.
The participial clause on encouraging crime carries the sentence's consequence, so crime in general gives criminal_justice (3.2, 5.2).
Corruption is one item in a series of the drug problem's effects (3.2); the balanced approach formula gives drugs only (5.2).
The clause claiming that organized crime exacerbates crime, terrorism, drugs and money laundering is a link claim, substantive for each (3.2, 5.1).
Peace across the Taiwan Strait names a specific dispute (4.10).
Illegal trafficking in small arms is one item in an enumeration of goals.
Small arms are not called illicit, and landmines are disarmament (4.4).
The debate on international enforcement against grave atrocities, prompted by the Gulf crisis, is collective security.
The linkage between financiers and the drug economy is a laundering channel and the main claim of its sentence (4.5); waste shipped into developing countries is waste crime.
'Held hostage' is a metaphor.
'Crime' said of the occupation is not criminal_justice.
Arbitrary arrests and improper detentions count whoever the victims, here only as items of an enumeration of violations (4.9, 3.2).
Support for implementing the Programme of Action against the illicit small arms trade is organized_crime (4.4); AIDS prevention involves no drug use.
The mafias appear only as a secondary object inside a relative clause about the country's record, so organized_crime is not added; the war on drugs is not peace.
Illicit small arms traffic gives organized_crime and disarmament gives peace (4.4).
Justice-system reform gives criminal_justice (4.9); the UNCAC resolution and the fight against corruption give corruption.
The risk that terrorists hold weapons of mass destruction is a claim of its own (4.6); the illicit small arms Programme of Action gives organized_crime.
Illicit small arms trade gives organized_crime whoever receives the weapons, and the sentence on arms fuelling African conflicts gives peace (4.4).
Irregular migrants falling victim to criminal organizations and dying is migrant smuggling by its kind (4.7); the clause carries the harm the sentence asserts.
Security challenges without a referent; peace appears only in the threat formula.
'Any crime' generalizes the response to terrorism, so criminal_justice is not added.
Bribery networks set up by a foreign Government's secret services are developed with their own actor and place (3.2, 4.5); the interference is not tied to an identifiable conflict.
Apartheid as a threat to peace is a formula, and the regime's 'crimes' are invective (4.10, 5.1).
The anti-money-laundering act and the ban on laundering the proceeds of crime are main claims (5.1).
The claim that these funds are used by terrorist groups and organized crime gangs is a link claim, substantive for each (3.2).
Resolution 1540 counts for terrorism by rule (4.6) although described only as non-proliferation; mediation and non-proliferation give peace.
Modern maritime piracy is organized_crime; prosecution is a means against it (5.1).
Incarceration for political opinions and torture of those persecuted count as arbitrary detention and ill-treatment (4.9).
Making drug trafficking an ICC crime is international criminal justice, so drugs only.
The sentence is devoted to specific crimes fuelling violence and criminality, a link claim substantive for each (3.2); crime in general gives criminal_justice.
Prevention and treatment of addiction is one item of a series of strategy components (3.2); weapons proliferation and terrorism are items of an enumeration of threats.
The commission against impunity is a justice-system mechanism (4.9); the peace process and MINUGUA give peace.
Transport and dumping of dangerous wastes in the region by unnamed actors and the ban on their import are waste crime (4.8); the non-proliferation regime gives peace.
Drug empires as the root of violence and terrorism is a drug-terror nexus about the organizations themselves (5.1); resolution 1373 is terrorism, not Council action on a situation.
The convention against illicit arms traffic is one item of a series of disarmament steps (3.2, 4.4).
Terrorism, extremism and illicit small arms trafficking are items of one enumeration of scourges (3.2); the African Peace and Security Architecture gives peace.
Rule of law in peacebuilding gives peace; the resolution on protecting diplomatic missions describes no attack, so no terrorism (4.6).
Small arms proliferation not called illicit gives peace (4.4); transnational crimes, money laundering and drug trafficking are items of one enumeration of sources of instability.
Crime in general is one item of a series of claims about migrants (3.2, 5.2); no smuggling is described.
Public security and violence as the people's main concern give criminal_justice; financial crimes and corruption appear only as items of series (3.2).
Drug traffic is the subject of a sentence and terrorism one item of its list of offences; overburdened domestic legal systems give criminal_justice, the ICC proposal does not (4.9).
Peace appears only as one value in an enumeration (4.10).
The use of force appears only in general terms and the aggression amendments are international criminal justice (4.9, 4.10); the diplomatic premises provisions describe no attack (4.6).
The supply-and-demand formula and addiction named as a problem give drugs only (5.2); violence associated with organized crime is one item of a series.
Extradition and the classification of political crimes are discussed for terrorism, so criminal_justice is not added.
Confiscating drug-related assets and new drug offences are drug control measures (4.1).
The use of force is criticized in general with no referent, and security appears only as a value (4.10).
The abductions are framed as a human-rights and bilateral issue rather than a conflict, and abduction by a State is not a terrorism act here (4.6, 4.10).
Captives and the kidnapping of reporters by a State in a war between States are peace only (5.2, row (b)).
Bringing terrorists to justice is enforcement against terrorism, so criminal_justice is not added.
Modern slavery and sexual violence in conflict are two examples of scourges (3.2).
The ICC and the crime of aggression are international criminal justice (4.9); peace appears only as one aspiration in an enumeration (4.10).
Corruption and fraud are items of a list of the former regime's practices (3.2); the killings in Syria give peace.
Grave violations against children in armed conflict are protection of civilians; abduction and recruitment are not framed as trafficking (4.7).
UN police to keep civil order and police training are police as institutions (4.9); Kosovo and UN missions give peace.
'Crime' by invading troops is not criminal_justice.
Prices and market access for farmers' legal crops as the remedy for coca and marijuana cultivation is a development alternative (4.3).
Small arms supply is not called illicit, so arms control gives peace only (4.4); rising crime rates give criminal_justice.
